transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this weekly facilities huddle started. We've got four operating areas that need generator power over the next 24 hours — the clinic, communications shelter, cold-storage point, and maintenance workshop — and only two generators, G-1 and G-2, which can't be run in parallel. Before I sign off on any schedule, I need each of you to report your current operating requirements. Medical, what does the clinic need? Signal, what's the comm shelter drawing? Facilities, what's the workshop load? And logistics, what's the cold-storage requirement? Let's hear it so we can build a plan that keeps everything running.

transcript.text: Col. Mercer, I need to flag something critical before we finalize any schedule. The clinic's vaccine refrigerator was moved to the G-1 circuit during a repair yesterday and must remain on G-1 continuously for the next 24 hours. I confirmed the connection with the clinic technician this morning, but this circuit change is not yet reflected on the facilities drawing. Whatever plan we build needs to account for the clinic being on G-1 without interruption.

transcript.text: Col. Mercer, for the communications shelter, I need to flag a critical scheduling constraint. The signal maintenance team sent me a notice this morning: we have a mandatory battery load test scheduled from 1000 to 1100 tomorrow, and the shelter must remain on G-2 throughout that entire test window. This is not yet reflected on the daily power slide, so it needs to be factored into whatever generator schedule we finalize today.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Col. Mercer, I need to flag a critical workshop constraint. The workshop's exhaust system inspection is booked for exactly 1400 to 1600 tomorrow, and the workshop must be running for that entire window. Additionally, the workshop circuit must be isolated from the cold-storage circuit during the inspection. I recorded the booking today, but this work window has not yet been entered into the generator schedule. We need to make sure the schedule accounts for the workshop being powered from 1400 to 1600 and that the cold-storage circuit is on a separate generator during that period.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Col. Mercer, I need to flag a critical fuel and generator constraint. The next fuel delivery arrives at exactly 1700 tomorrow, and our fuel on hand only supports G-2 for 16 operating hours. To preserve communications and clinic continuity, G-2 must be scheduled offline from exactly 0100 to 0900 tomorrow. The workshop should remain on G-1 after its inspection window. I received the carrier confirmation this morning, but the revised fuel timing has not yet been posted to the power plan. This needs to be factored into whatever schedule we finalize today.

transcript.text: Good input from everyone. Let me lay out the schedule as I see it and identify the one open decision. Here's what the constraints give us: G-1 runs continuously with the clinic on it for the full 24 hours. G-2 is offline from 0100 to 0900, then comes back online. The comm shelter is on G-2 from 1000 to 1100 for the battery load test. The workshop inspection runs 1400 to 1600 with the workshop on G-1 and cold-storage on G-2 during that window. After inspection, the workshop stays on G-1. Now, the gap Maj. Alvarez flagged is real — during the 0100 to 0900 window when G-2 is offline, cold-storage loses power if it's normally on G-2. We have two options: either we put cold-storage on G-1 during that window, which means G-1 would be carrying the clinic, cold-storage, and possibly the workshop simultaneously, or we accept a cold-storage outage from 0100 to 0900. Before I decide, I need to address the load capacity concern that CW2 Brenner and Maj. Alvarez both raised. Neither of them has individual load numbers for the workshop or cold-storage. Do any of you have the kilowatt ratings for each operating area? G-1 and G-2 are both 60-kilowatt generators, so I need to know the combined draw before I sign off on putting multiple loads on a single generator. Without those numbers, I can't confirm that G-1 can safely carry the clinic plus workshop, or clinic plus cold-storage, without risking a shed of the clinic circuit — and Maj. Sato has made clear that cannot happen. Someone needs to get me those load figures before I finalize this schedule.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Col. Mercer, I can speak to the clinic's load. The vaccine refrigerator on G-1 draws approximately 1.5 kilowatts — that's the critical load I'm concerned about. I don't have the kilowatt ratings for the other three operating areas, so someone from facilities, signal, or logistics will need to provide those. But I want to be clear: whatever combined load ends up on G-1, the clinic circuit cannot be shed at any point during the next 24 hours. If the numbers come back showing G-1 would be overloaded with clinic plus workshop plus cold-storage during the 0100 to 0900 window, then my recommendation is to accept a cold-storage outage rather than risk shedding the vaccine refrigerator. Those vaccines are irreplaceable and a power interruption would compromise the entire stock.
